pages.title: What you will learn
pages.body:
> 🔢 **Strand 1 — Number**
Counting, calculating and reasoning with numbers — the language of trade, science and everyday life.

> 🎯 **Content standard** (B9.1.3)
- B9.1.3.1 — Apply the understanding of operations on fractions to solve problems involving fractions of given quantities and round the results to given decimal and significant places.

> 🎯 **In this chapter you will learn to:**
- review equivalent fractions, simplest form, mixed numbers and improper fractions
- carry out mixed operations on fractions
- use BODMAS/PEDMAS with whole numbers, powers and fractions
- solve word problems involving fractions and percentages

pages.title: Reviewing fractions
pages.body:
> 🎯 **You will learn to:** Review fractions and solve problems involving basic operations on fractions.
Curriculum indicator B9.1.3.1.1
## ✏️ Example 3.1
a) [[3/4]] of a circle is shaded. Shade the same fraction of a rectangle divided into 12 equal squares. b) Write three fractions equivalent to [[10/15]]. c) Express [[45/60]] in its simplest form. d) Express [[27/5]] as a mixed number. e) Express 2[[7/9]] as an improper fraction.
[[fig:m9-f05]]
Figure 3.1: [[3/4]] of the circle = [[9/12]] of the rectangle
**Solution**
a) [[3/4]] = [[9/12]], so shade **9** of the 12 squares.
b) e.g. [[2/3]]**,** [[4/6]]**,** [[20/30]]
c) HCF 15: [[3/4]]
d) 5[[2/5]]
e) [[2×9+7/9]] = [[25/9]]
## ✏️ Example 3.2
Work out: a) [[3/4]] + [[7/8]] b) 1[[1/2]] + [[4/5]] − [[5/6]] c) [[2/3]] × [[3/4]] − [[3/8]] d) [[5/8]] ÷ 2[[1/2]] + [[2/3]]
**Solution**
a) [[6/8]] + [[7/8]] = [[13/8]] = 1[[5/8]]
b) LCM 30: [[45/30]] + [[24/30]] − [[25/30]] = [[44/30]] = 1[[7/15]]
c) [[1/2]] − [[3/8]] = [[1/8]]
d) [[5/8]] × [[2/5]] = [[1/4]]; [[1/4]] + [[2/3]] = [[11/12]]

pages.body:

2. Simplify: a) 2[[3/4]] + 1[[5/6]] b) 4[[1/3]] − 2[[3/5]] c) [[3/7]] × 1[[5/9]] d) 3[[3/4]] ÷ 1[[7/8]]

pages.title: Mixed operations and BODMAS
pages.body:
> 🎯 **You will learn to:** Add and/or subtract, multiply and/or divide given fractions using the order of operations (BODMAS or PEDMAS), and apply the understanding to solve problems.
Curriculum indicator B9.1.3.1.2
> 🔑 **Key idea: PEDMAS** — **P**arentheses → **E**xponents (powers and roots) → **D**ivision and **M**ultiplication from left to right → **A**ddition and **S**ubtraction from left to right.
## ✏️ Example 3.3
Simplify: a) 3^{4} ÷ 3^{2} + 40 − 2^{3} × 3^{2} ÷ 9 b) 18 ÷ 6 × (4 − 3) + 6 c) 18 ÷ 3^{2} × (4 − 3) × 10
**Solution**
a) Exponents: 81 ÷ 9 + 40 − 8 × 9 ÷ 9 = 9 + 40 − 8 = **41**
b) Parentheses: 18 ÷ 6 × 1 + 6 = 3 + 6 = **9**
c) 18 ÷ 9 × 1 × 10 = 2 × 10 = **20**
## ✏️ Example 3.4
Simplify: a) [[2/3]] × [[3/4]] − [[5/8]] ÷ 2[[1/2]] b) [[3/4]] ÷ [[3/8]] + ([[4/5]] − [[1/2]]) c) ([[3/4]] + [[5/8]]) × [[4/11]] − [[1/2]]
**Solution**
a) Multiply and divide first: [[2/3]] × [[3/4]] = [[1/2]]; [[5/8]] ÷ [[5/2]] = [[1/4]]. Then [[1/2]] − [[1/4]] = [[1/4]]
b) [[3/4]] × [[8/3]] + [[3/10]] = 2 + [[3/10]] = 2[[3/10]]
c) [[11/8]] × [[4/11]] − [[1/2]] = [[1/2]] − [[1/2]] = **0**

pages.title: Word problems involving fractions and percentages
pages.body:
> 🎯 **You will learn to:** Review word problems involving basic operations on fractions.
Curriculum indicator B9.1.3.1.3
## ✏️ Example 3.5
A test has 20 questions. How many questions must you answer correctly to score 80%?
**Solution**
80% of 20 = [[80/100]] × 20 = **16 questions**
## ✏️ Example 3.6
By what percentage was a television set reduced if it was marked GH₵2,250 and sold for GH₵2,025?
**Solution**
Reduction = 2,250 − 2,025 = GH₵225.
Percentage reduction = [[225/2250]] × 100% = **10%**
## ✏️ Example 3.7
In an election with two candidates, one candidate claimed 52% of the votes and the other claimed 2,681 votes. If 5,000 people voted, how do you know the claims are invalid?
**Solution**
52% of 5,000 = 2,600 votes. Then 2,600 + 2,681 = **5,281**, which is **more than the 5,000** people who voted. The claims cannot both be true. (Equivalently, 2,681 votes is 53.6%, and 52% + 53.6% > 100%.)
## ✏️ Example 3.8
Esi's orange drink was [[2/5]] orange squash and Fusena's was [[5/12]] orange squash. Whose drink tasted stronger of orange?
**Solution**
[[2/5]] = [[24/60]] and [[5/12]] = [[25/60]]. Since [[25/60]] > [[24/60]], **Fusena's drink** was stronger (41.7% squash compared with 40%).

pages.title: Exercise 3.3
pages.body:
> ✏️ **Exercise 3.3** — try these on paper or in your head, then tap **Quick check** to see the answers.
1. Akua scored 54 out of 75 in a test. Express this as a percentage.
2. A trader bought a radio for GH₵450 and sold it for GH₵540. Find her percentage profit.
3. A school had 1,250 learners. The number increased by 12%. How many learners are there now?
4. [[3/8]] of a farm is planted with cassava, [[1/3]] of the rest with maize, and the remaining 15 hectares with vegetables. Find the area of the farm.
5. A shirt priced at GH₵180 is reduced by 15%, and the new price is then increased by 15%. Is the final price GH₵180? Explain.

parts.a: No: 180 × 0.85 = 153; 153 × 1.15 = GH₵175.95. The 15% increase is calculated on a smaller amount.

pages.title: Chapter 3 summary
pages.body:
- Change mixed numbers to improper fractions before multiplying or dividing.
- Follow PEDMAS/BODMAS: brackets, powers, ×/÷ left to right, +/− left to right.
- Percentage change = [[change/original]] × 100%.
